description: Land Acquisition to Address Saltwater Intrusion on Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. As saltwater intrusion causes tidal freshwater forests to transition to brackish marsh, swallow-tailed kite nesting grounds and black bear habitat will decrease. By pairing strategic acquisitions with the nature-based solution of assisted wetland migration, habitat connectivity is ensured and human well-being is supported by intentionally using the land to meet community needs. Coverage: Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge (2024). The toolkit gives Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
